questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of profit satisficing?
options: Aiming for enough profit to be satisfied rather than the maximum possible
Aiming for the largest possible profit
Deliberately making a loss
Reinvesting all profit into the business
questions.why: Satisficing is a deliberate choice to trade potential profit for something else, usually time, simplicity or control. It explains a great deal of real small business behaviour.
whyNot: That is profit maximisation.
Satisficing still means a satisfactory profit, not a loss.
That is reinvestment, a separate decision.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: setting up a business whose main aim is to address a social or environmental problem?
options: Social entrepreneurship
Intrapreneurship
Profit maximisation
Independence
questions.why: A social enterprise trades and earns revenue, but profit is the means rather than the end, and most of it is reinvested into the purpose.
whyNot: Intrapreneurship is entrepreneurial behaviour inside an existing business.
Profit maximisation is the opposite priority.
Independence is the motive of wanting to be your own boss.

questions.stem: Which of these is a non-financial motive named in the specification?
options: Independence
Profit maximisation
Profit satisficing
Cost efficiency
questions.why: The four non-financial motives are an ethical stance, social entrepreneurship, independence and home working. Independence is consistently one of the most commonly given reasons for starting a business.
whyNot: A financial motive.
Also a financial motive, just a moderate one.
A business objective rather than a personal motive for starting.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a characteristic and a skill for an entrepreneur?
options: Characteristics are largely who you are; skills can be learned or hired in
Characteristics can be learned; skills cannot
They mean the same thing
Skills apply only to managers
questions.why: Resilience and initiative are traits. Financial literacy and negotiation are capabilities. The distinction matters because a founder lacking a skill can learn it or hire it, rather than failing.
whyNot: This reverses the two.
They are distinct, and a question may ask for either specifically.
Entrepreneurs need skills too, arguably more of them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of an ethical stance?
options: A set of moral principles guiding how a business trades, even where it reduces profit
Obeying the law in every country the business operates in
Donating profits to charity each year
Paying the lowest legal wage
questions.why: An ethical stance goes beyond legal compliance to a moral position the business holds even at a cost, such as paying suppliers fairly or refusing certain materials.
whyNot: Legal compliance is the minimum. An ethical stance goes further.
Donation is one possible expression of it, not the definition.
That would be cost minimisation rather than an ethical position.

questions.stem: A guesthouse owner could profitably open a second property but chooses not to, in order to keep their weekends. What does this illustrate?
options: Profit satisficing
Profit maximisation
Social entrepreneurship
Cost efficiency
questions.why: They are trading potential profit for time, which is satisficing. It is a rational choice given their objectives, and treating it as a failure of ambition misreads what they want.
whyNot: Maximisation would mean opening the second property.
There is no social purpose described here.
Cost efficiency is about unit costs, not about whether to expand.

questions.stem: Why is financial literacy such an important skill for an entrepreneur?
options: Profitable businesses still fail if they run out of cash
It removes the need for an accountant
It guarantees the business will be profitable
Lenders do not require financial information
questions.why: Profit and cash are different things. A business can be profitable on paper and still be unable to pay wages, which is why cash flow understanding is the skill that most often decides survival.
whyNot: It helps the founder understand the accounts; professional help is still usually needed.
Understanding the numbers does not by itself create profit.
Lenders require detailed financial forecasts.

questions.stem: Why is it a mistake to recommend rapid expansion to an owner whose motive is independence?
options: Expansion usually means debt, investors or delegation, all of which reduce their independence
Expansion always reduces profit
Independence and profit are the same thing
Small businesses cannot legally expand
questions.why: The recommendation has to match the owner's objective. Growth typically requires finance and shared control, which is exactly what someone motivated by independence set out to avoid.
whyNot: Expansion often raises profit. The conflict here is with independence, not profitability.
They are different, and can pull in opposite directions.
There is no such restriction.

questions.stem: How can an ethical stance also be commercially advantageous?
options: It can open premium markets and protect the business from reputational damage
It always lowers the cost of materials
It removes the need to pay tax
It guarantees higher sales volume
questions.why: Certification and a credible ethical position can give access to buyers willing to pay more, and it insures against the revenue loss a supply chain scandal causes. So ethics does not always cost.
whyNot: Ethical sourcing usually raises input costs.
No connection to tax liability.
It may raise volume in some markets and reduce it in price-led ones.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of resilience in an entrepreneur?
options: The ability to recover from setbacks and continue
The willingness to take large financial risks
The ability to see what needs doing without being told
Confidence in dealing with customers
questions.why: Most businesses hit a serious problem within two years, so the ability to absorb a setback and keep going is what distinguishes those that continue.
whyNot: That is risk-taking, a separate characteristic.
That is initiative.
That is self-confidence.
